# 黃帝陰符經註解--鄒訢

**ID:** KR5a0125
**Custom ID:** ZB5a0125

## Authors / Editors
- 鄒訢 1130 - 1200
- WYG 陰符經考異

**Editions:** SJB, ZHDZ

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A ten-folio commentary attributed in the Daozang heading to Zōu Xīn 鄒訢, a Daoist from Kōngtóng 崆峒 (where the Yellow Emperor reportedly discoursed with Guǎngchéngzǐ 廣成子 on the meaning of the *Yīnfú jīng*; cf. [DZ 120 preface](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0120)). Zōu Xīn is a pseudonym of Zhū Xī 朱熹 (1130–1200): during the Warring States period, Zōu 鄒 was the name of a state earlier called Zhū 朱; and *xīn* 訢 is synonymous with *xī* 熹 (cf. *[DZ 1001 Zhōuyì cāntóng qì](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a1002)* 3.8a). The present work is identical with the commentary in Zhū Xī's *Yīnfú jīng kǎoyì*.

The real authorship is revealed by Huáng Ruìjié 黃瑞節 in his compilation *Zhūzǐ chéngshū* 朱子成書 (preface dated 1305): the explanations are not by Zhū Xī himself (he only revised the text) but by his friend and collaborator Cài Yuándǐng 蔡元定 (1135–1198). Cài used the long version of the *Yīnfú jīng* (446 characters), dividing it into three *piān* 篇; the disputed final part is left uncommentated. Huáng Ruìjié's supplementary notes quote additional sources and point out textual variants in four different *Yīnfú jīng* versions (8a).

This same commentary-text appears separately in the Daozang at *[DZ 118 Huángdì yīnfú jīng zhù (Cài shì)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0118)*.

**Abstract**

Hans-Hermann Schmidt, in Schipper & Verellen eds., *The Taoist Canon* (2004) 2:698 (§3.A.1), dates the edition to c. 1305. The frontmatter brackets composition notBefore 1198 (Cài Yuándǐng's death — earliest plausible composition by the student) / notAfter 1305 (Huáng Ruìjié's edition), with dynasty 南宋—元. Zōu Xīn (= Zhū Xī) is the catalog-meta person wikilinked.
